scope: Documented capabilities and explicitly qualified scale evidence; not implementation certification

columns.title: PRP L3
columns.profile: PRP wire-v4, protected adjacency and E2E 0x0202; local bootstrap, known identities; privacy mechanisms enabled; C08: interior transit between intermediaries, no endpoint rendezvous/deeper-session termination or optional traffic-history logging

columns.title: PRP over IP
columns.profile: IPv4 / UDP / PRP wire-v4, protected adjacency and E2E 0x0202; numeric peers, known identities; privacy mechanisms enabled; independent deployment uses private IPv4; C08: interior transit between intermediaries, no endpoint rendezvous/deeper-session termination or optional traffic-history logging G01 global deployment: conventional globally routed IPv4/UDP over the BGP Internet, matching IP/MQ and round119 BP/LP/I2/GN. Private IPv4 deployments remain separate S03 capabilities; adjacent-only IP meshes are not this global witness. This does not change native PRP L3.

columns.title: IP (IPv4/IPv6)
columns.profile: IPv4 or IPv6 datagram service / ICMP; numeric destinations; no application TCP/UDP/TLS/QUIC or IPsec, NAT or stateful firewall; optional transit traffic-history/export disabled. Global unicast control: TCP / BGP-4 + MP-BGP. F12: IGMP/MLD + PIM-SM. Independent deployment: RFC 1918 private IPv4 or locally generated IPv6 ULA, locally provisioned routes. Global Internet allocation remains a separate requirement. F09: optional per-packet unicast next-hop rotation over provisioned multiple routes (RFC 2991), not merely flow-hashed ECMP; G04: multiple BGP reflector clusters and group-scoped PIM RPs.; C06: separate IPv6 client contexts with distinct randomized temporary sources under a shared multi-host prefix, no stable source/DNS identity or host-identifying flow-label policy reused; no continuity or on-link anonymity claim

columns.title: Secure DTN
columns.profile: IPv4 / TCP / TLS 1.3 / TCPCLv4 / BPv7 + BPSec; independent private IPv4 and RFC 9758 private-use ipn domain; known EIDs, aggregate gateway exits, locally agreed dtn collective names, numeric peers; participant-operated CAs, local trust and BPSec keys, NODE-ID validation, no online OCSP or SNI; optional TLS padding, concurrent proactive forwarding and static collective fanout credited architecturally; independent logical-node EIDs/certificates/BPSec keys per context, no cross-context TLS resumption; discard completed bundles, no retained report archive or transit traffic history G01 global deployment: conventional BGP-routed IPv4 Internet underlay, matching the IP/MQ global case; private deployments remain separate S03 capabilities. F21: ION native BPSec receive-API witness at 154a4cc7354b26661169f8d8b75a4002cd509a9f; exact source-EID/key bindings, distinct pairwise HMAC keys held only by each original sender and receiver, BIBs over primary and payload, primary-inclusive payload integrity scope; application treats bundleSourceEid as authenticated only when both native verification indicators are true. No application authentication exchange, group key or relay-held origin key; no F16 admission/revocation guarantee inferred. F16 alternative witness: ION 154a4cc with optional BSL 468db9b enabled and mandatory APPOUT wildcard-source BIB verification over primary and payload. One authorized remote sender at a time; a fresh secret key is held only by that sender and the final receiver, never transit. Native policy uses a locally fixed key-registry identifier. Revocation uses completed shutdown of receiver and consumers, a fresh empty bundle/fragment/delivery store and a fresh key provisioned only to the newly authorized sender. No hot revocation, simultaneous independent-key allowlist, or claimed source-EID authentication is inferred from this witness; F21 retains its separate exact-source policy.

columns.title: DTN / CGR–SABR
columns.profile: IPv4 / TCP / TLS 1.3 / TCPCLv4 / BPv7 + BPSec, with CGR routing procedures from SABR CCSDS 734.3-B-1 (2019). Documentary composition; executable integration not yet qualified. Locally provisioned numeric peers, private IPv4, private-use ipn identifiers (RFC 9758), singleton destinations, supplied contact/range plans and local clocks. Participant-operated certificate trust with NODE-ID validation, no online OCSP, DNS or SNI dependency. Final-pair BCB-AES-GCM payload protection and BIB-HMAC-SHA2 verification with locally provisioned pairwise keys; no relay-held final keys. No application authentication wrapper, anonymity overlay, multicast extension or shared-reference directory. BPv7 mapping of SABR priority/critical metadata and custody-dependent behavior remains an explicit integration question, not silently credited. BPv7 source witness: ION 154a4cc7354b26661169f8d8b75a4002cd509a9f for native final-source delivery and origin-side critical-bundle replication. Exact-origin pairwise keys, primary and payload integrity coverage, and application checks of both verification flags are required. This pins these BP-layer mechanisms only; complete TCPCL/TLS or LTP/Encapsulation/AOS integration, critical metadata propagation at later hops, custody mapping and simultaneous on-wire path use remain unqualified. F16 bounded configuration: F16 alternative witness: ION 154a4cc with optional BSL 468db9b enabled and mandatory APPOUT wildcard-source BIB verification over primary and payload. One authorized remote sender at a time; a fresh secret key is held only by that sender and the final receiver, never transit. Native policy uses a locally fixed key-registry identifier. Revocation uses completed shutdown of receiver and consumers, a fresh empty bundle/fragment/delivery store and a fresh key provisioned only to the newly authorized sender. No hot revocation, simultaneous independent-key allowlist, or claimed source-EID authentication is inferred from this witness; F21 retains its separate exact-source policy. This final BP delivery gate is independent of the chosen CGR route and TCPCL ingress. C06 capability witness uses separate logical contexts with independently provisioned private-domain EIDs, certificates, BPSec keys and stores; no cross-context TLS resumption or common certificate subject/serial is required.

columns.title: DTN / LTP
columns.profile: BPv7 + BPSec / LTP RFC 5326 / Encapsulation Packet Protocol 133.1-B-3 / AOS virtual-channel packet service 732.0-B-4 (2021 documentary baseline, not latest edition); CGR/SABR 734.3-B-1 routing. LTP segment binding follows 734.1-B-1 Annex B. No UDP, IP, TCPCL or TLS. Bidirectional adjacent links, locally supplied contact/range plans, peer/engine mapping, clocks and keys; singleton BP endpoints. All-red block transfer selected; optional green-part service is not credited. Final-pair BCB-AES-GCM and BIB-HMAC-SHA2 protect payload and authenticate a configured remote security source; no relay-held final keys. No link encryption/SDLS, anonymity overlay, application authentication wrapper or independent-participant discovery directory. Executable bindings, BPv7/SABR metadata mapping and allocation rules remain unqualified. CCSDS mission conformance and unrestricted local engine/channel assignment are not asserted. BPv7 source witness: ION 154a4cc7354b26661169f8d8b75a4002cd509a9f for native final-source delivery and origin-side critical-bundle replication. Exact-origin pairwise keys, primary and payload integrity coverage, and application checks of both verification flags are required. This pins these BP-layer mechanisms only; complete TCPCL/TLS or LTP/Encapsulation/AOS integration, critical metadata propagation at later hops, custody mapping and simultaneous on-wire path use remain unqualified. Identity witness for independent deployment: private-use ipn EIDs confined to one administrative domain, with locally generated pairwise BPSec keys and exact-EID receiver policies. EID uniqueness and key distribution are configured by the participants; no public-key self-certification, automatic trust or global uniqueness is claimed. This does not settle AOS SCID allocation in S03. F16 bounded configuration: F16 alternative witness: ION 154a4cc with optional BSL 468db9b enabled and mandatory APPOUT wildcard-source BIB verification over primary and payload. One authorized remote sender at a time; a fresh secret key is held only by that sender and the final receiver, never transit. Native policy uses a locally fixed key-registry identifier. Revocation uses completed shutdown of receiver and consumers, a fresh empty bundle/fragment/delivery store and a fresh key provisioned only to the newly authorized sender. No hot revocation, simultaneous independent-key allowlist, or claimed source-EID authentication is inferred from this witness; F21 retains its separate exact-source policy. This final BP delivery gate is independent of the chosen CGR route and LTP ingress. It does not qualify the complete LTP/Encapsulation/AOS executable binding.

columns.title: libp2p
columns.profile: IPv4 / UDP / QUIC (TLS 1.3) / libp2p; known numeric peers and Peer IDs, migration enabled; independent deployment uses private IPv4; separate logical peer keys/stores per context, no resumption, NAT or transit flow logging; no pubsub F16: final Peer ID allowlist through ConnectionGater plus coordinated closure of all revoked-peer connections. G01 global deployment: conventional BGP-routed IPv4 Internet underlay, matching the IP/MQ global case; private deployments remain separate S03 capabilities.

columns.title: Tor onion service
columns.profile: IPv4 / TCP / TLS / Tor + onion service v3; public Tor directory system; persistent filesystem client authorization enabled; transit traffic-history logging disabled; optional Conflux proposal-329 onion-service linking/resumption credited as design, not verified deployment; F21: client identity delivered to the receiving onion service; reverse service authentication is distinct F16: authorization-file removal plus Tor restart; retain authorization for permitted clients or stop the service when none remain.

columns.title: I2P
columns.profile: IPv4 / TCP / NTCP2 / I2P destinations and tunnels; locally supplied fresh RouterInfo bundle, numeric NTCP2 contacts and known destination keys; multiple active outbound tunnels with at least two remote hops, tunneled destination lookups; correct local clock; no online reseed or external naming service; isolated router/destination key contexts without shared family declarations; independent private IPv4 with i2np.allowLocal and local bootstrap/network configuration; concurrent-tunnel policy is architectural, ordinary Java per-pair selection is sticky; transit-only C08 role with optional identity-bearing traffic/debug history disabled G01 global deployment: conventional BGP-routed IPv4 Internet underlay, matching the IP/MQ global case; private deployments remain separate S03 capabilities.

columns.title: Yggdrasil
columns.profile: IPv4 / TCP / TLS 1.3 / Yggdrasil / IPv6 / application UDP; optional TLS padding credited architecturally; numeric peers, pinned keys, numeric application destinations; independent deployment uses private IPv4; independent logical-node keys and TLS contexts, no cross-context resumption; transit traffic-history logging/export disabled; ordinary TCP only, no MPTCP or custom scheduler; Ironwood pinned to d50055b11f5ec5b56ee4e56ba9a75261461821dc; G01: connected mesh of adjacent-only private-IP peerings, no Internet transit or remote public peers; F21: applications on native node addresses, not devices behind routed subnets; trusted local receive interface

columns.title: cjdns
columns.profile: IPv4 / UDP / cjdns / IPv6 / application UDP; ordinary application path without custom route-label overrides; outer point-to-point CryptoAuth enabled; numeric peers, known keys/local credentials, numeric application destinations; independent deployment uses private IPv4; independent logical-node keys and non-identifying peer credentials per context; transit traffic-history logging/export disabled; C02 includes documented DHT lookup role; no selected cover-traffic policy; private peering credentials, no public beacon advertisement; replicated route-server design with TCP/HTTP/WebSocket announcement exchange, independent servers and numeric contacts; C08 covers transit forwarding, not route-server query caches; F21: applications on native cryptographic node addresses, no imported IP tunnels; trusted local receive interface

columns.title: Multipath QUIC
columns.profile: IPv4 / UDP / QUIC (TLS 1.3) + multipath-21, optional proactive same-offset STREAM copies on two validated paths; numeric peers, locally generated certificates explicitly trusted by counterparts, mutual handshake authentication, no SNI requirement or online certificate service; independent private IPv4 deployment; separate trusted context keys, no cross-context tickets/token reuse, NAT or transit flow logging F16: local final-key allowlist, all-connection close on revocation, resumption and 0-RTT disabled.; G01 global deployment: conventional BGP-routed IPv4 Internet underlay; private deployment remains a separate S03 capability

columns.title: SCION
columns.profile: IPv4 / UDP underlay / SCION / application UDP; numeric topology, daemon, control/discovery and endpoint addresses, locally provisioned trust and correct local clock; no end-to-end TLS; independent UDP end-host address/flow contexts within an AS; transit traffic-history logging/export disabled

columns.title: Reticulum
columns.profile: Reticulum 1.5.5 / Link over serial interfaces; secret IFAC enabled, credentials not publicly advertised; no local TCP sharing or IP interfaces; no LXMF; regional transport-node distribution; no application cover-traffic policy; F21: native Link.identify enabled; identity-dependent actions wait for verified identification; G01: connected serial mesh with recursive_prs enabled on transport interfaces C08: Reticulum 1.5.5 standalone serial transport with the entire --config directory on private verified noswap tmpfs; no host swap/hibernation/dumps, snapshots, durable logs or exporters. Seed only clean static config/local identity/IFAC credentials; do not restore learned paths, announces or participant activity. Cold starts relearn routes. This supersedes the earlier C08 stock-disk profile; RAM activity remains observable.

columns.title: Basic Nostr
columns.profile: IPv4 / TCP / TLS 1.3 / HTTP Upgrade / WebSocket / NIP-01; optional TLS padding credited architecturally; WSS relay hostnames resolved through DNS; regular events proactively published concurrently over two independent relay paths; separate author contexts; no NIP-17/44/42 or secret-gated camouflage; F21: verified event author to reader, not live publishing connection or relay identity; G01 global deployment: WSS relays over conventional BGP-routed IPv4 Internet C08: operator-controlled nostr-rs-relay at b5c1f642e4f4c3b9c54f5d18d66f4c53642076b4, SQLite in_memory=true, bundled URI-enabled SQLite and memory temporary storage; no file logging, persistent WSS-proxy logs, diagnostics export, swap, dumps, hibernation or snapshots. Apply to both selected relays. Regular events remain in RAM until discarded/restart; other readers/relays can retain copies.

columns.title: Meshtastic
columns.profile: Meshtastic firmware v2.8.1.8e6a88d Alpha (commit 8e6a88d06f44cad26f1e8d7cd402939ccacb9b4c); standalone LoRa mesh, radio/region preset agreed locally, ordinary CLIENT relaying; no MQTT, Wi-Fi/Ethernet network or Internet bridge; trusted local serial client. PKI-capable build, direct messages with independently confirmed endpoint public keys; private channel key, STRICT signature policy, no licensed plaintext mode. Store-and-forward module disabled. No claim that this Alpha is a production recommendation; radio nodes are the cryptographic endpoints. C04 witness fixes ordinary CLIENT rebroadcast_mode=ALL; private-channel key and STRICT signature policy retained. Unknown-channel opaque forwarding is included, not CLIENT_MUTE/NONE. F16 administrative witness: headless CLIENT, KNOWN_ONLY plus STRICT, locally provisioned authorized User records/full keys only, no remote administrative authority for ordinary peers; store-forward off, persisted ignore policy and completed restart for revocation. Separate from C04 CLIENT/ALL probe witness. C06 witness: native meshtasticd/Portduino with real LoRa radio, separately provisioned full contexts, explicit distinct General.MACAddress values, independent keys/names/preferences and no shared identifier-bearing telemetry. No automatic embedded-device rotation claim or UDP radio transport. C08: native Linux meshtasticd with real SPI/USB LoRa, ordinary CLIENT/ALL relaying, full writable virtual filesystem on verified private tmpfs with noswap; host swap/hibernation/dumps and persistent log/export/backup paths disabled. Restore only clean static identity/radio/trust provisioning at cold start, never learned NodeDB/history. No flash-device default or live-memory secrecy claim.

columns.title: GNUnet / CADET
columns.profile: IPv4 / UDP TRANSPORT plugin / CORE / CADET; R5N discovery. GNUnet v0.20.x handbook is the explicit documentary baseline, not a claim about the latest release. Numeric private-IP neighbors, locally supplied HELLO contacts and known peer public keys; no online hostlist, DNS, NAT helper, GNS, file-sharing or Messenger service. Runtime version and discovery/bootstrap configuration remain to be qualified. G01 global deployment: conventional BGP-routed IPv4 Internet underlay, matching the IP/MQ global case; private deployments remain separate S03 capabilities. C08 witness: GNUnet 0.20.0 legacy UDP, proportional ATS, heap dhtcache with DISABLE_BF_RC=YES, peerinfo NO_IO=YES, logging NONE without forced overrides; fresh service state, no optional traffic archive/TNG, bootstrap contacts supplied again after restart. F16 witness: dedicated CADET endpoint with no local listening ports; locally initiated bidirectional channels only to an administratively selected set of peer public keys. Revocation uses a completed cold restart of the local CADET service and its consuming clients, discarding old channel/IPC delivery state before recreating channels only to the updated set. No application payload validator, external firewall or incoming-channel acceptance callback is credited. This is a controlled receiver/subscriber configuration, not an incoming server allowlist or uninterrupted hot revocation.

columns.title: NDN / NFD
columns.profile: NDN packet format v0.3 / NFD 24.07 with direct Ethernet faces and local Unix-socket applications; no IP face, DNS discovery or public testbed enrollment. Known content/key names, local FIB configuration and local trust anchors; ECDSA P-256 Data signatures validated by the consumer. No content-encryption extension, mandatory signed consumer Interests, application sync/group protocol or DTN extension. Data-producer authentication is distinct from live peer authentication. F18 witness: positive-capacity CS with admission/serving enabled, solicited staged cache transfers, bounded contacts before eviction/freshness expiry; no custody or restart durability claim. G01 witness: connected tree of direct Ethernet adjacencies; native multicast v5 strategy at /, root-prefix next hops to every neighbor, and local producer registrations only. Known globally scoped names, no forwarding hints, NLSR, global directory or IP underlay. Interest lifetime/hop budget covers the tree diameter; provision resources for the offered load. This flooding construction establishes reachability, not G05 capacity or efficient routing.

columns.title: AX.25 / NET/ROM
columns.profile: AX.25 v2 / classic NET/ROM network and transport circuits over direct radio/serial links; known callsigns/SSIDs, locally configured routing ports and NET/ROM announcements. Historical protocol description plus Linux AX.25 port configuration; no IP encapsulation, TCP/IP payload service, BBS mailbox or added cryptography. Executable version not yet qualified. S01/S03/C06 credit the private direct-serial role with locally provisioned labels; no claim about radio licensing or public callsign acceptance.

columns.title: batman-adv
columns.profile: Linux 6.12 batman-adv / native Ethernet frame service, direct Ethernet-style links; no IP application, VPN underlay, WPA/MACsec or end-to-end security layer. Locally administered MAC addresses, local interface attachment and trusted local client; This is an L2 service boundary, not an IP application stack. Round118 witnesses: BATMAN_IV, native bonding enabled for F09, gateway mode off, network coding not credited; shared-code IV/V findings identified per cell.

columns.title: IP / Babel
columns.profile: IPv6 datagram service / ICMPv6; control plane IPv6 / UDP / Babel RFC 8966. Independent locally assigned ULA prefixes, provisioned interfaces, numeric destinations; no DNS, TCP/QUIC, IPsec, NAT, external firewall, Babel DTLS/MAC extension or added application authentication. Babel is the selected routing control plane; no BGP/global Internet composition silently added. G01 constructive witness: administratively provisioned binary IPv6 hierarchy inside a locally assigned ULA /48, with direct routed adjacencies. Each router originates only its own aggregate backed by a local discard route; upward advertisements contain that aggregate, downward advertisements only the root /48. Exact-prefix/interface input and output filters suppress remote specifics. Connected leaf LANs override their local aggregate. No BGP, directory, automatic aggregation controller or global leaf-prefix catalog is introduced. Fixed hierarchy and address assignment are required; this is not arbitrary Internet topology or G05 capacity.

columns.title: IPv6 IoT / RPL
columns.profile: 6LoWPAN (RFC 4944/6282) / IPv6 / RPL (RFC 6550, non-storing downward routing with RFC 6554, OF0 RFC 6552) / UDP / DTLS 1.3 (RFC 9147). IEEE 802.15.4 link binding; endpoint leaf role, participant-operated RPL root and routers. Locally provisioned ULA prefix, numeric peer addresses, 6LoWPAN neighbor discovery RFC 6775. RPL unsecured mode on an access-controlled link; DTLS does not protect routing control. End-to-end DTLS with distinct locally provisioned pairwise external PSKs, psk_ke and TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256; no 0-RTT, tickets or application authentication overlay. Fresh PSK handshakes allowed; no forward-secrecy claim for this PSK-only choice. No DNS, public CA, cloud broker, CoAP or MQTT dependency. No DTLS-terminating gateway: the final peers hold the traffic keys. Documentary composition; complete executable integration and sleep/overhead behavior remain unqualified.

columns.title: HIPv2 / ESP
columns.profile: IPv4 / HIPv2 control (RFC 7401) and ESP-protected user traffic (RFC 7402), with host mobility RFC 8046. Independent deployment uses private IPv4, known numeric initial locators and pinned peer Host Identities/HITs; locally generated ECDSA P-256 identities, ECDH P-256, HIP ECDSA/SHA-384 HIT suite 2 and ESP AES-128-CBC with HMAC-SHA-256 (transform 8). Ordinary application UDP is carried inside the protected host-to-host data path, not as a HIP underlay tunnel. No DNS, rendezvous service, external CA, NAT-traversal extension or application authentication wrapper is selected. One moving endpoint with a reachable known peer; no simultaneous-mobility guarantee. Documentary composition; exact executable integration remains unqualified. G01 global deployment: conventional BGP-routed IPv4 Internet underlay, matching IP, PRP-over-IP and Multipath QUIC. Independent private deployment remains the separate S03/S04 capability; adjacent-only private IP meshes are not this global case.

columns.title: CCNx 1.0
columns.profile: IPv4 / UDP / CCNx 1.0 semantics RFC 8569 and TLV encoding RFC 8609. Independent deployment uses private IPv4, numeric adjacent forwarders, locally configured name-prefix FIB entries and known content names. Producer Content Objects use ECDSA-SHA256 signatures with locally generated keys explicitly trusted by consumers; no externally mandated name registry or certificate authority selected. Interests use CRC32C integrity checks, not authenticated consumer identities. In-network matching, pending Interests and caching follow CCNx semantics. No TLS, encrypted-session extension, application authentication wrapper or NDN/NLSR extension is added. Dynamic routing and automatic global name discovery are not silently supplied by static FIB configuration. Documentary composition; executable integration remains unqualified. G01 global deployment: conventional BGP-routed IPv4 Internet underlay, matching IP, PRP-over-IP and Multipath QUIC. Independent private deployment remains the separate S03/S04 capability; adjacent-only private IP meshes are not this global case.

columns.title: LISP
columns.profile: IPv4 / UDP / LISP (RFC 9300 data plane and RFC 9301 control plane) / inner IPv4 / application UDP; configured EID prefixes and RLOCs; numeric peer and mapping-service addresses; participant-operated Map-Resolver and Map-Server with locally provisioned registration keys. No LISP-SEC, endpoint TLS/IPsec, or application identity layer selected.

columns.title: ILNPv6
columns.profile: ILNPv6 / TCP with ILNP identifier-only transport binding (RFC 6740 and RFC 6741); IPv6-compatible packet format with distinct 64-bit Identifier and Locator semantics, not an outer IPv6 tunnel; RFC 6743 Locator Updates and RFC 6744 Nonce Destination Option; locally generated NIDs, Router Advertisements and neighbour discovery; DNS NID/L64 discovery per RFC 6742. Host mobility between authorized attachments with overlap, a stationary reachable correspondent, and unchanged NIDs during the TCP connection. No IPsec, TLS, CGA identity binding or multipath TCP selected. Experimental specification; executable composition not qualified.

criteria.title: Operates without IPv4/IPv6 throughout the stack
criteria.definition: No mandatory IP layer, including operational support.
criteria.research_action: Fix non-IP binding, bootstrap and support dependencies; run without IP.

criteria.title: Needs no participant IP address configuration
criteria.definition: Participant-facing addressing uses a self-generated address or a non-IP participant namespace; no assigned participant IP address is needed at that layer. Underlay and relay transport IP configuration are excluded uniformly and remain assessed by F01/F03. This is not zero-configuration deployment: other identifiers, peers, trust and permissions may need provisioning.
criteria.research_action: Trace endpoint creation and bootstrap; distinguish application and underlay configuration.

criteria.title: Routed operation needs no topology-dependent address configuration
criteria.definition: No network-prefix, subnet or locator assignment tied to attachment in the selected stack, including its underlay. DHCP/SLAAC automate such configuration rather than remove it. Locally generated identities and session-local forwarding labels do not count. Excludes route policy, trust, permissions and physical/link setup.
criteria.research_action: Trace address assignment across the selected stack; distinguish topology-dependent locators from self-generated identities and local forwarding labels. F02 concerns participant provisioning; F03 concerns the routed network as a whole.

criteria.title: Cryptographic reference independent of location
criteria.definition: Participant or service reference verifiable independently of its locator; not necessarily self-certifying.
criteria.research_action: Trace reference creation and key binding; distinguish identity, certificate and locator.

criteria.title: Peer continuity and authorization across sessions
criteria.definition: A peer continuity and authorization context survives the end of a session and a change of carrier. No particular object name, data structure or protocol-specific lifecycle is required. A stable identity key alone does not establish retained authorization context.
criteria.research_action: Establish what peer continuity and authorization state survives session termination and carrier changes, and how it is reused for a later session. Evaluate documented behavior regardless of implementation terminology; a stable key alone is insufficient.

criteria.title: Encrypts content between communicating endpoints
criteria.definition: Protection between the compared endpoints, not merely a transit link.
criteria.research_action: Fix the end-to-end profile and key custody; identify every encryption termination point.

criteria.title: Cryptographically authenticates a remote participant
criteria.definition: Remote identity or signed authorship proof; does not imply civil identity, mutual authentication or current presence.
criteria.research_action: Specify whose identity is proved, to whom, and whether proof covers a live session or stored message.

criteria.title: Preserves a transport connection across path changes
criteria.definition: The same connection survives; reconnecting with the same contact does not qualify. UDP alone has no connection.
criteria.research_action: Define address/path change and connection lifetime; test continuity, replay and reordering.

criteria.title: Uses simultaneous paths for one communication
criteria.definition: Concurrent useful data paths, rather than sequential failover or probes.
criteria.research_action: Fix scheduler, path policy and extension; distinguish multiple sessions from one communication.

criteria.title: Proactively duplicates data across distinct paths
criteria.definition: Intentional redundancy before loss, rather than retransmission after loss.
criteria.research_action: Find replication and deduplication rules; test physically diverse paths and resource costs.

criteria.title: Retains messages for delivery after disconnection
criteria.definition: Deferred delivery storage, not transient transport buffers.
criteria.research_action: Check persistence, expiry, capacity and recovery without a contemporaneous path.

criteria.title: Multicast replication at network forwarders
criteria.definition: One-to-many network forwarding; application-relay fanout does not qualify. BP selects static collective fanout with implementation qualification pending.
criteria.research_action: Fix multicast routing and replication; distinguish broadcast, flooding and application pubsub.

criteria.title: Group with multiple authorized senders and continuity across sessions
criteria.definition: Multiple authorized participants can send to a group. Membership and group authority are distributed, and group continuity is independent of individual session lifetimes. Matching terminology or a particular implementation is not required.
criteria.research_action: Identify sender authorization, membership and distributed authority rules; trace group continuity across session termination and subsequent participation. Apply the same behavioral requirements to every selected stack.

criteria.title: Explicit goal of concealing endpoint location
criteria.definition: Location-hiding mechanism; not immunity to global correlation.
criteria.research_action: Define observer and profile; inventory visible identity, adjacency and location metadata.

criteria.title: Isolates resources under distributed DoS
criteria.definition: Preserves specified minimum legitimate service under a bounded adversary.
criteria.research_action: Fix adversary budget and bottlenecks; measure admission, goodput, latency, CPU, memory and queues.

criteria.title: Controls final-peer access without external firewall
criteria.definition: Final-peer network payload admission: allow locally authorized cryptographic peers, deny others before application payload delivery, and revoke old authority at a completed local cutover, including active paths and pending delivery. Native policy hooks and administrative teardown/restart are allowed; authorized service must remain available after cutover. Already delivered data, application-operation permissions, handshake/probe traffic, unrelated host services and DoS isolation are outside scope. Added application authentication or payload filtering is not credited.
criteria.research_action: Trace native final-peer admission and revocation at completed local cutover; see round063.html#policy.

criteria.title: Operates without DNS
criteria.definition: No DNS from bootstrap through authorized traffic; names absent from packets alone are insufficient.
criteria.research_action: Fix peers, discovery, certificates and dependencies; initialize without DNS queries.

criteria.title: DTN forwarding across discontinuous contacts
criteria.definition: Network intermediaries retain and later forward an admitted item across non-overlapping contacts, without a contemporaneous complete end-to-end path. A mailbox at a common server, transport buffering or reconnection alone does not qualify. Previously established trust and bounded expiry are allowed.
criteria.research_action: Trace A-to-B followed by B-to-C with no overlapping contacts, intermediate storage, expiry, cryptographic viability and duplicate handling; distinguish architecture from executable activation.

criteria.title: Transit forwarding without per-end-to-end-flow state
criteria.definition: Transit can forward without a mandatory entry for each end-to-end flow or circuit. Routes, neighbor sessions and aggregate multicast state are allowed. Endpoint transport state is outside this transit-only test. Include selected overlay relays, not only the IP underlay.
criteria.research_action: Inventory every selected transit role and its state keys/lifetimes. Distinguish aggregate routes and neighbor sessions from endpoint-flow/circuit entries and optional caches.

criteria.title: Authenticated final-peer identity available to the application
criteria.definition: The selected stack authenticates the final communicating peer and exposes that identity to the receiving application bound to the communication, without an added application authentication exchange. Neighbor identity, unauthenticated addresses or an unbound claim are insufficient. This does not supply civil identity, account roles, permissions or transit anonymity.
criteria.research_action: Trace proof validation, application-visible identity and binding to the received channel/item. Separate final peer from relays, object authors and security sources; inspect close/rekey and stale-reference behavior.

criteria.title: Shared-reference discovery of independent participants
criteria.definition: One shared reference can discover multiple independently identified participants, without an exclusive controller of that reference or a shared private identity. A bounded candidate set is sufficient; exhaustive enumeration and simultaneous delivery are not required. Only mechanisms in the declared stack count. Self-declaration does not establish membership legitimacy, service authorization or current availability.
criteria.research_action: Trace reference formation, independent declarations, multi-candidate lookup and candidate identity binding. Separate routing fanout, anycast and content retrieval from participant discovery; do not silently add a discovery application or module.

criteria.title: Endpoint mobility without infrastructure routing control
criteria.definition: Supports an endpoint changing attachment or access network while preserving its peer identity and ongoing logical communication, without requiring the application to establish a new peer relationship or reconstruct communication. The endpoint must not need administrative control of infrastructure routes, prefix origination or an AS; moving an administratively controlled network with the endpoint does not qualify. Normal participant attachment, path authentication and automatic protocol signaling are allowed, including signaling intrinsic to a mesh or overlay; merely running routing code does not disqualify a participant. Ordinary network access permission is not authority to originate infrastructure routes. Evaluate a supported endpoint role and state its limits; client-only support can qualify. Mere route repair with stationary endpoints, or retaining an identifier while restarting communication, is insufficient. Lossless handover, simultaneous mobility of both endpoints and indefinite disconnection are not required. Only mechanisms in the declared stack count.
criteria.research_action: Move an ordinary participant between attachments with no new infrastructure route/prefix/AS privileges. Trace retained identity and communication state, automatic locator/path updates and application-visible behavior. List access permissions separately from routing authority. Exclude administrator-driven prefix/AS relocation. Record role, interruption, loss and timeout; test existing runtime qualifications separately.

criteria.title: Endpoint operation with planned sleep periods
criteria.definition: An endpoint may suspend all transmission and reception for a declared interval and subsequently resume authorized communication using retained identity/configuration and permissions supplied by the selected stack, without mandatory communication during sleep or renewed manual enrollment. Fresh transport sessions, route discovery and cryptographic handshakes on wake are allowed and must be disclosed. Evaluate an endpoint, not a forwarding role. This does not require preserving a live connection, receiving commands while asleep, or intermediate message storage. Owner-approved clarification: F24 asks whether the endpoint resumes without renewed manual enrollment, preserving the identity/configuration and permissions actually supplied by the selected stack. Cryptographic final-peer authorization is not required when the stack does not provide it; no such security capability is inferred.
criteria.method: Documentary plausibility under the approved 24-hour workload
criteria.research_action: Owner-approved reference: an endpoint suspends all transmission and reception for 24 hours, then exchanges a 256-byte useful message with one previously authorized peer. Fresh discovery, routing and cryptographic establishment are allowed. No traffic budget was approved. Retain valid identity/policy and distinguish fresh establishment from live-session continuity. Evaluate configured authorization lifetime and required wake-up repair. No energy or overhead claim. Owner-approved clarification: F24 asks whether the endpoint resumes without renewed manual enrollment, preserving the identity/configuration and permissions actually supplied by the selected stack. Cryptographic final-peer authorization is not required when the stack does not provide it; no such security capability is inferred.

criteria.title: Bounded protocol overhead for sporadic communication
criteria.definition: After 24 hours with the endpoint radio silent, exchange 256 useful bytes with one previously authorized peer. Retain provisioned identity, configuration and valid trust, but expire sessions and learned neighbor state. The budget is 65,536 bytes total endpoint-interface transmit plus receive, including selected-stack control, discovery, fresh establishment, framing and useful data, through delivery. Assume no losses and one hop to access. Infrastructure is available; its traffic not crossing this endpoint interface is outside this metric. This is a bounded documentary configuration witness, not an energy measurement, global traffic bound or guarantee for every configuration.
criteria.research_action: Count all endpoint-facing traffic for a complete selected-stack witness; preserve unresolved components explicitly.

criteria.title: Recovers after one path is blocked
criteria.definition: One operator drops a path; another reachable, authorized path has capacity. Reconnection and interruption are permitted.
criteria.research_action: Block one laboratory path; measure recovery, loss and discovery dependence on that path.

criteria.title: Conceals the final destination from the first intermediary
criteria.definition: A non-colluding intermediary sees its decrypted state and traffic. Excludes direct endpoint communication.
criteria.research_action: Inventory keys, fields, control queries and forwarding tables; check final identity and location exposure.

criteria.title: Conceals protocol control fields in established traffic
criteria.definition: Passive observation of established protected traffic, excluding bootstrap. Assess exposed control fields and protocol markers; timing/volume inference is separate. This is not a claim of complete protocol indistinguishability.
criteria.research_action: Map cleartext and encrypted established-packet fields, including outer framing; do not use initial bootstrap exposure as a negative.

criteria.title: Includes a defense against active-probe identification
criteria.definition: An uncredentialed adversary probes an endpoint and observes replies and timing; no endpoint compromise.
criteria.research_action: Define valid, invalid and replay probes; inspect disclosures before authorization against a control service.

criteria.title: Bootstraps while external DNS is unavailable
criteria.definition: Initial state as specified in the column, with no DNS cache. Does not cover blocking all peers or directories.
criteria.research_action: Disable DNS before process startup; inventory discovery and trust. F17 is the corresponding functional capability.

criteria.title: Includes access-level cross-session unlinkability
criteria.definition: Capability to avoid a compulsory persistent participant-identity link across sessions. Excludes bootstrap, known subscriber attachment and timing/volume inference. Optional identity reuse does not negate the capability.
criteria.research_action: Identify stable identifiers and support for distinct identities across contexts; distinguish a compulsory identity link from user-selected reuse and timing inference.

criteria.title: Includes a defense against entry/exit correlation
criteria.definition: Includes a mechanism that reduces observable timing/volume information for cooperating observers. Optional padding or cover traffic can qualify; effectiveness and deployment defaults are separate, and complete correlation prevention is not required.
criteria.research_action: Identify padding, batching, mix or cover mechanisms and their scope; separately measure correlation reduction and cost under a fixed observer model.

criteria.title: Needs no persistent history of final identities
criteria.definition: A transit operator or relay supplies stored state after communication. Capability requires operation without persistent author/destination history.
criteria.research_action: Inspect memory, disk, backups, telemetry and default logs; separate required, optional and derivable data. This is not a legal retention ruling.

criteria.title: Communication without a mandatory separate authority
criteria.definition: Willing peers can communicate from local information without a separate mandatory naming, routing, identity, governance or ledger authority. Network directory authorities and domain certification roles count; counterpart admission policies do not. Underlay allocation is assessed separately.
criteria.research_action: Identify any indispensable third-party approval, registry, consensus signer or trust anchor in the selected network. Test direct operation without that external service.

criteria.title: Participant identity requires no external issuer
criteria.definition: Participants generate a usable cryptographic identity locally; counterparties decide whether to trust or authorize it. Does not imply civil identity.
criteria.research_action: Trace key creation, reference registration and acceptance; determine whether an issuer must authorize creation.

criteria.title: Selected stack needs no external address/name allocation
criteria.definition: Independent deployment needs no public address allocation, DNS delegation or externally assigned domain identifier. Private/local addressing may qualify; Internet reachability is a separate requirement.
criteria.research_action: Fix deployment boundary, private/public underlay and name resolution; inventory allocator and delegation dependencies.

criteria.title: Independent operation under participant-controlled administration
criteria.definition: Participants can deploy and maintain an operational domain with all mandatory control, trust and coordination components under their own administration, without authorization or an indispensable operational service from a specific external vendor or operator. Locally operated authorities are allowed, as is direct peer operation without such authorities. Choosing among external service providers alone does not qualify. This does not guarantee global reachability, freedom from external address allocation, seamless migration or immunity from a local administrator.
criteria.research_action: Inventory bootstrap, enrollment, trust renewal, naming, routing, discovery and coordination dependencies in the selected composition. Establish whether participants can operate all mandatory services and trust roles themselves. Distinguish optional outsourced services from fixed vendor activation, mandatory public directories or external approval. Keep address/name allocation in S03, issuer-free identities in S02 and absence of any separate mandatory authority in S01. Preserve the selected deployment: do not substitute a private clone of a declared public network.

criteria.title: Global reachability without complete global reachability tables
criteria.definition: The complete selected stack permits global reachability without requiring a complete global reachability table at transit nodes or control services. Include prefix, identity and other identifier reachability, and required underlay routing. Moving that table upstream or into a directory does not qualify. Partitioned state is allowed; this is not zero state or a quantitative capacity guarantee.
criteria.research_action: Inventory every transit and control role, including discovery, upper aggregators and the underlay. Establish how arbitrary reachable destinations are located without a mandatory complete global table. A local default route, local labels or a small private deployment alone are insufficient.

criteria.title: Local repair without mandatory global dissemination
criteria.definition: A documented local attachment change can be repaired within an affected scope without notifying every node. Not a guarantee for every failure.
criteria.research_action: Trace local repair and propagation, including underlay; identify cases requiring wider updates.

criteria.title: Discovery without a complete catalog at every node
criteria.definition: Scoped services or recursive queries permit discovery without a global catalog at every node. Does not bound rendezvous or backbone costs.
criteria.research_action: Trace cold lookup, state placement, publication updates and cache-miss fanout.

criteria.title: Scale-out without a fixed-capacity coordination point
criteria.definition: Added infrastructure can distribute routing/discovery work without an obligatory single fixed-capacity coordinator. Decentralization alone is insufficient.
criteria.research_action: Map complete-stack coordination dependencies, partitioning, replication and failure recovery.

criteria.title: Global scale with bounded discovery and overhead
criteria.definition: One connected network of at least 10 billion devices on contemporary equipment, evaluated in an agreed reference deployment calibrated to regional Internet interconnections and participant concentration. Existing destinations unknown to the origin: protocol-attributable discovery delay below 1 s; new participants discoverable across regions within 1 h. At least 99.9% of attempts meet deadlines, counting failures/timeouts. Control and unsolicited traffic below 5% of a 1 Gbit/s domestic access per direction. Required routing state below 64 GB per transit equipment, not per endpoint; distributed state and growing aggregate network memory are allowed, without a mandatory complete participant table at any one equipment. Include all required stack layers and declared load, ingress and mobility. At least 1,000 distinct destinations accessed per device per day, independently of concurrent payload activity; cold-origin and warm-cache cohorts must be explicit. See round174.html.
criteria.method: Model and validation against approved operational limits
criteria.research_action: Validate the approved limits simultaneously under declared cross-region workloads. Keep protocol processing, queueing, timers, retries and extra exchanges in discovery delay; subtract only a preregistered minimal physical-medium baseline and report total elapsed time too. Count all routing-essential structures per transit equipment across processes. No global monetary or aggregate-memory ceiling. Missing evidence is Pending, not No. Yes/No concerns the agreed regional reference deployment; missing evidence remains Pending. See round174-daily-destinations.json.

criteria.title: Public interoperability between independent implementations
criteria.definition: At least two independently developed implementations exchanged traffic for the selected profile in a publicly documented test. Shared standardization work does not negate implementation independence; two wrappers around the same core do not qualify. Credit only tested functions.
criteria.research_action: Identify implementers, code lineage, versions, selected profile, exchanged functions and a public test report; distinguish an interoperability goal from a completed test.

criteria.title: Published independent security analysis
criteria.definition: A third party has published a security audit or formal analysis of security-critical mechanisms of the selected profile. Identify analysis type, scope, assumptions, version and conflicts of interest. Paid independent review can qualify; publication does not imply a clean result or complete security.
criteria.research_action: Find the actual report and authorship; distinguish implementation audit, protocol analysis and formal verification. Confirm coverage of the selected composition rather than only an underlying primitive.

criteria.title: Public open-source implementation of the selected profile
criteria.definition: At least one publicly obtainable implementation covers the selected profile with its necessary implementation components available under OSI-approved licenses. Official reference status is not required. Public specifications or partial demonstration code alone do not qualify.
criteria.research_action: Locate public code, exact version, license texts, dependencies and supported profile scope. A private checkout or absent implementation files in a specification mirror does not decide public availability.

criteria.title: Published reproducible independent measurements
criteria.definition: An independent party has published at least one quantitative measurement of the selected profile with versions, configuration, method and results sufficient for reproduction. State exactly what was measured; one result does not qualify all performance or scale claims.
criteria.research_action: Identify independent execution and reproducible artifacts; list measured latency, wire overhead, mobility or other metric and workload. Distinguish theoretical header size from measured traffic.

criteria.title: Documented sustained operation by independent operators
criteria.definition: At least one independent organization or community has operated the selected profile with real users for at least six months. Six months is this study's declared adoption threshold, not a technical guarantee. Research-only demonstrations do not qualify.
criteria.research_action: Find public operator evidence, role, profile/version, deployment dates and real-user scope. Independence does not require a commercial ISP; do not infer operation from download counts.

criteria.title: Unprivileged routine endpoint operation
criteria.definition: A supported ordinary endpoint can perform the selected communication on an identified general-purpose OS without root/admin or equivalent elevated networking capabilities during routine operation. Disclose any privileged installation, provisioning or helper; those are not silently counted as unprivileged runtime.
criteria.research_action: Pin OS/version, endpoint role, executable, capabilities and helpers. Separate install/configure privileges from sustained operation. An untested adapter or UDP binding alone does not decide this criterion.

criteria.title: Operation without an additional kernel module
criteria.definition: A supported endpoint operates on an identified general-purpose OS without installing an additional kernel module or rebuilding its kernel. Stock networking modules and drivers are allowed; disclose required OS features and configuration.
criteria.research_action: Verify implementation installation/runtime dependencies and stock-OS support. Distinguish userspace architecture from a tested deployment and kernel configuration from an additional module.

criteria.title: Operation without specialized hardware
criteria.definition: A supported endpoint can execute the selected profile on commodity computing/network hardware, without a mandatory specialized radio, accelerator or secure element. Ordinary NICs are allowed; identify carrier constraints and do not replace the selected stack.
criteria.research_action: Document hardware requirements and a supported endpoint configuration. Optional accelerators do not negate the capability; mandatory physical-link hardware must remain in scope.

criteria.title: User-controlled identity creation without network administration
criteria.definition: Over an already authorized and provisioned transport, an ordinary user can create and use additional independently controlled communication identities without network-administration privileges or modifying shared interface addresses, prefixes or routes. Identity creation must not require per-identity host-network reconfiguration or administrator provisioning. Peer acceptance and transport-access permissions remain separate. This does not promise unlimited resources, anonymity, or isolation from all resource contention.
criteria.research_action: Trace identity generation, custody and protocol use for a second ordinary user. Identify any per-identity privileged operation, shared address/interface mutation or administrator allocation. Credit only identity mechanisms in the selected stack; an extra application authentication layer is not implicit. Separate this architectural capability from D01 full endpoint runtime privileges, F03 topology-dependent addressing and S02 external identity issuance.

criteria.title: Post-quantum end-to-end key establishment
criteria.definition: The selected end-to-end key-establishment construction provides documented post-quantum confidentiality against recorded-traffic decryption, using a suitable post-quantum KEM or justified hybrid construction. Identify algorithms, combiner, negotiation and downgrade conditions. This alone does not establish post-quantum authentication against active attackers.
criteria.research_action: Inspect the actual selected key-establishment suite, not identity-signature options. Verify hybrid composition and negotiation; distinguish passive confidentiality from authentication and overall protocol security.

criteria.title: Unrestricted use and implementation of the specification
criteria.definition: The publicly available specification permits use and implementation for any purpose, including commercial use, without field-of-use restrictions or individual permission. Attribution and redistribution obligations must be disclosed. Modification does not imply compatibility, conformance or endorsement. This does not require permission to republish altered normative prose as an official standard, and does not assess patent rights (L02) or implementation-code licensing (E03). Cover the required layers of the selected profile.
criteria.research_action: Verify authoritative use/implementation permissions across the selected specification layers; distinguish notices and compatibility claims from restrictions on use. Assess patent grants separately in L02.

criteria.title: Declared royalty-free patent commitment
criteria.definition: An attributable holder declaration or published commitment explicitly offers royalty-free implementation of the selected profile for applicable claims under the declaring holder's control. A recorded direct holder declaration is admissible for every project; publication or registry entry is reported separately, not required for Yes. State attribution, scope, conditions and publication status. This assesses the declared policy, not execution or enforceability of a patent license, third-party patent clearance, or copyright permission. An express patent grant attached to the selected implementation is admissible within its stated Work or contributor-version scope; it is not a promise covering every independent reimplementation. The same holder-bounded rule applies to direct declarations and public grants.
criteria.research_action: Obtain a dated attributable holder declaration or applicable public grant; identify scope, conditions and publication status. Do not infer a commitment solely from open development, copyright licensing or IETF participation.

RFC 8446 sections 4.2.11 and 6.2 distinguish binder verification from access control: even a valid PSK can be denied. Retain this record when discarding session traffic keys, then apply the same decision to a fresh handshake after reattachment through another authorized, reachable carrier. Admission is indexed by the provisioned peer context, not the old IP/port tuple. This is a documentary capability inference from native external-PSK and admission mechanisms, not from key stability alone.

The later session uses fresh traffic secrets. Link access, neighbor discovery and routing must separately restore reachability. This does not establish seamless handover, automatic peer discovery, crash persistence or an executed full RPL/DTLS stack. No new runtime test occurred. Six fresh-process native ingress fixtures now include valid 16-byte IFAC, native queues/workers, real identity/path learning and temporary cache. Paced and burst results distinguish immediate learned paths from held announces; held packets have already passed signature validation. A corrupted IFAC control is rejected. Input comes from an in-memory receive-only interface with socket creation forbidden, not a serial medium or full forwarding topology. Release/expiry, service under attack and scale capacity remain unqualified. Valid-IFAC synthetic traffic assumes interface authorization; it is not evidence that an outsider without the IFAC secret can reach this processing path. The next fixture observes the same 64-destination burst through native release scheduling without new arrivals, clock acceleration, forced release or changed timers. Its timeline distinguishes delayed eventual route learning from immediate loss. This single isolated run cannot establish loaded convergence, serial capacity or a service floor. The ingress held-announcement map is distinct from the capped outgoing announce queue; their limits and aging rules must not be conflated. A separate two-run 300-destination fixture reaches the native 256-entry hold limit; unretained destinations at that observation are not a proof of permanent unreachability. Three follow-up fixtures recover all 42 previously unretained destination path entries after native local explicit requests and supplied valid IFAC path responses; an unsolicited-response control remains blocked. Native outgoing requests are captured and decoded before replies are supplied. This establishes conditional local recovery, not discovery by a remote responder, multihop convergence or query capacity. Recursive request propagation has additional limits and is not exercised. Native request_path tests now distinguish local and recursive calls under a genuinely populated outgoing announce queue and its timer. Recursive calls emit nothing while gated, whereas a local nonrecursive call emits with that queue occupied. After drain, the remaining cap interval still gates recursion; a new call succeeds after the interval. The blocked function calls do not register pending requests or emit later by themselves in this observation. Higher-level retries and actual multihop discovery remain outside this fixture. Three independent RNS processes now demonstrate an actual native query from A through B to C, a native response generated at C, and encrypted SINGLE payload delivery A-B-C. A and B begin without the target path, and C does not proactively announce. Whole IFAC frames are passed unchanged through harness pipes with no direct A-C edge, shared routing state or fabricated response. This closes the previous functional remote-response gap for one tiny unloaded topology only; serial capacity, congestion, churn and global scaling remain unqualified. Nine additional fresh chains pass at enforced 2400, 9600 and 115200 bit/s. Native HDLC escaping and flags are accounted at ten bits per byte (8N1); whole IFAC frames are delivered only after their scheduled serialization finishes. This adds finite-rate functional discovery and encrypted delivery evidence, but uses unloaded software queues rather than physical UARTs. It does not qualify discovery capacity, congestion, churn, hardware budgets or global scale. A further bounded-queue experiment submits sixteen distinct destination requests in one burst over a 9600-bit/s chain, with three repetitions each at 256, 1024 and 8192 wire-byte queue capacities per direction. It separately records harness tail drops, emitted native frames, discovery coverage after twelve seconds and exact encrypted payload delivery during a subsequent eight-second phase. Caller retries are absent. Incomplete discovery at the observation deadline is not permanent unreachability, and queue capacity alone is not a model of native recursive-request admission. This remains a small synthetic workload, not a contemporary-hardware global-capacity qualification. All nine runs discovered one of sixteen destinations and delivered its payload. At 8192 bytes all sixteen requests reached B without laboratory drops, but only one native request was emitted toward C. Thus the observed coverage limit cannot be attributed solely to finite link buffers; exact native branch attribution and paced/retry recovery remain untested in this round.

cells.reason: A bounded native configuration closes the unmatched-source gap without an application filter. Enable ION BSL and install two APPOUT wildcard-source/wildcard-destination verifier rules: require BIB-HMAC-SHA2 over primary and payload, using the locally configured active pairwise key, with delete_bundle on failure. All accepted source EIDs match the policy, so inventing an unlisted source cannot bypass it. The rule creates a required security operation before any matching BIB is found; absent BIBs leave security-block number zero, whose canonical-block lookup fails. Invalid or absent results cause non-success finalization and mark the bundle insecure; ION abandons it before delivery. Query errors also return before delivery. The remote key holder is the only authorized remote sender in this witness; keys are not given to transit. Revocation is a completed cold cutover: stop receiver and consumers, retire all old delivery/fragment/storage state from the active instance, replace the key with an independently fresh secret shared only with the newly authorized sender, then resume. Old in-flight bundles fail the new key; old admitted queues and callbacks cannot survive the fresh instance. Authorized new traffic can pass the same native verifier. F16 explicitly allows administrative teardown/restart. This is a capability proof for one authorized sender at a time, not a default ION behavior, live multi-peer revocation, claimed-EID identity proof, or preservation of queued data. F21 is unchanged.

cells.reason: A constructive native configuration resolves F16 without treating an application message validator as an admission gate. The dedicated receiver opens no CADET listening port and creates bidirectional channels only toward locally authorized peer public keys. channel_create passes the exact destination to the service; the channel belongs to that destination tunnel, whose key derivation includes its public identity. Validated plaintext is looked up in the channel map of that tunnel, not a global channel-number namespace. Unsolicited incoming channels at unopened ports remain unbound; the native plaintext-data handler drops data when neither local owner nor destination client exists. Thus an authorized remote peer can send payload on the locally initiated channel, while another peer cannot acquire the same local delivery path merely by choosing the same port or channel number. For revocation, stop the consuming clients and local CADET service, wait for termination, discard the old volatile delivery/channel state, and restart with no listening ports and channels only to the revised authorized set. This completed cutover removes active and queued delivery authority; authorized communication resumes on new channels. F16 permits administrative restart and does not require remote initiation or uninterrupted availability. This does not establish a general incoming-server allowlist, live channel-revocation safety or a tested GNUnet deployment. The earlier connect-callback lifetime and optional MQ-validator limitations remain valid but are not used by this witness.

cells.reason: A bounded staged-pull witness carries the same named signed Data from producer A through caches B and C to final requester D. First, a local requester at B solicits the item from A; B admits the returning Data. Disconnect A-B. During B-C contact, a local requester at C asks for the same name; B serves its CS and C admits the returned Data. Disconnect B-C. D subsequently requests it from C. There is never an A-to-D path. Forwarder lookup, cache-hit response and solicited-Data insertion compose this relay-to-relay transfer without an application mailbox or new wire protocol. This is demand-triggered cache forwarding, not autonomous push, custody transfer or guaranteed delivery. The channel PSK is a shared access/encryption credential, not a shared private identity. The full channel configuration, not its short packet hash alone, is the reference. This is bounded radio-mesh discovery, not arbitrary global alias lookup. A node number or display name alone is not a cryptographic identity; key confirmation for subsequent sensitive direct messages remains required by the selected profile.

cells.reason: Relationship continuity is separated from volatile carrier locators and paths. Section 7 specifies authenticating a replacement path, binding it to the existing relationship/direction/generation, validating it, migrating eligible work and draining the old path. Connection aliases, service lanes, ordering, replay and item identities remain unchanged when handover continuity is claimed. This supports moving attachment while preserving the relationship, provided a replacement path is obtainable and authorized. Failure to prove continuity must fail or create a new epoch, not silently pretend continuity. Architectural credit does not demonstrate a carrier-specific mobility controller, automatic discovery at every access point or interruption-free operation.

cells.reason: A mobile bundle endpoint can retain its EID and pending bundles while changing access contacts. Under a policy that retains rather than fails pending forwarding, BP permits later forwarding without application resubmission. A bounded witness uses provisioned numeric contacts at both attachments and the same NODE-ID credentials: the convergence-layer TCP/TLS session can be rebuilt without replacing the bundle identity or application endpoint. The selected NODE-ID authentication separates that identity from a changing IP locator. Credit concerns continued bundle delivery, not TCP stream migration or automatic discovery of an arbitrary new contact. Retention policy, reachability and bundle lifetime remain conditions.

cells.reason: A bounded planned-mobility witness qualifies under the existing F23 criterion, consistently with F23-BP. A mobile bundle endpoint keeps its EID, final-peer BPSec keys and pending bundle store while leaving access node A and later attaching to access node B. Both contacts, their native link bindings and the onward path to the same destination are provisioned before movement. SABR sections 2.2-2.3 represent changing adjacency with timed contacts between stable node numbers and compute routes from those plans, without requiring the mobile participant to originate infrastructure prefixes or modify the infrastructure during the move. RFC 9171 sections 5.4 and 5.4.1 permit retaining pending forwarding and resuming it when forwarding becomes possible. The original pending application data is delivered without application resubmission. The new contact establishes the selected TCPCLv4/TLS 1.3 connection using provisioned numeric peers and the retained NODE-ID credentials. A new convergence-layer session does not replace the BP endpoint or pending bundle identity.

cells.qualification: This is a documentary constructive inference for scheduled movement and retained bundle delivery, not arbitrary-access discovery, seamless stream migration, lossless handover or an executed integrated-stack test. Require live persistent BP state, adequate storage, a retain-not-fail policy, bundle lifetime beyond the next contact, usable preprovisioned native links and correct schedules/clocks. An expired or deleted bundle is not recovered by this witness. No critical-bundle replication, custody extension or SAGA/IPND discovery is needed. The earlier demand for a live discovery adapter was too broad for this planned-contact role; its integration gaps remain relevant to unplanned mobility and E03, but do not block this architectural F23 Yes. No profile, criterion or external routing authority is added. TCPCL reconnection and any partial-transfer restart remain below the application. No claim that a TCP connection survives changing IP attachment.

Buffered missing data can be retransmitted, including after both legs disappear, preserving the logical stream. This supplies an architectural mobility witness; it does not establish deployed Tor support. Section 2.7 explicitly says full resumption is not supported in C-Tor. Retained endpoint state, adequate buffering and a reachable service are required; memory pressure or unrecoverable loss can terminate the set.

cells.reason: A co-located client/router can retain its Destination and local I2CP session while changing external NTCP2 access. With UDP transport disabled, NTCPTransport accepts external-address updates and rebuilds RouterInfo separately from the local client session. TunnelPool replaces failed tunnel leases, while ClientConnectionRunner requests updated LeaseSets using existing SessionParams. This supplies a bounded witness with overlapping reachable access and timely replacement tunnels, without recreating the application Destination session. It does not preserve the old external TCP connection or establish streaming continuity: no streaming extension is selected. Retained router/client processes and usable peers at the new access are prerequisites.

Keep the local I2CP session alive, introduce the new access, renew multi-hop tunnels and leases, then remove the old access. Verify unchanged Destination/session ID and continuing message exchange without CreateSession. Measure losses and deadlines; test total tunnel loss and repeated LeaseSet negotiation failure, which can disconnect the client. No experiment performed.

Routing resolves paths toward that identity independently of the underlying TCP/TLS peering addresses; the documented design explicitly handles node mobility. With the process, TUN interface and application UDP endpoint retained, path replacement need not recreate the application peer relationship. The witness uses reachable, preconfigured adjacent numeric peers in the selected private mesh; it does not import public peers or automatic peer exchange. This is architectural credit, not a measured handover or a guarantee that every interruption is survivable.

cells.reason: A moving native cjdns endpoint can retain its key-derived IPv6 address and inner CryptoAuth session while its path labels change. getSession looks up the existing session by IPv6 identity and updates its path rather than allocating a new cryptographic session. cells.reason: Constructive direct-Ethernet/static-FIB witness: retain the provisioned producer key and content name, use a fresh Interest and signed Data with 256 content bytes. Bound each complete Name TLV to 64 bytes. Interest including Nonce, lifetime and hop limit is at most 83 bytes. Data with empty MetaInfo, P-256 DER signature at most 72 bytes and a bounded KeyLocator is at most 477 bytes. Allow another 64 bytes of local-link envelope per packet and 38 Ethernet byte-times per packet: at most 764 total, below 65,536. There is no network session to resume or certificate to fetch in this preprovisioned-key witness.

cells.reason: The already selected private direct-serial role admits a bounded wake-up witness. Linux 6.12 NET/ROM splits each 256-byte useful message into 236+20-byte fragments; its 15-byte network and 5-byte transport headers keep the larger packet within AX.25 paclen 256. Count fresh AX.25 and NET/ROM connection setup, four data frames for one message in each direction, transport and link acknowledgments, two small announcements and conservative shutdown/maintenance reserves: 32 frames total. A generous 512-byte frame cap, KISS command byte, worst-case doubling by escaping, delimiters and 8N1 start/stop bits yield 41,120 byte-equivalents, below 65,536.

cells.source_label: Linux 6.12 NET/ROM, AX.25 and MKISS source; original KISS protocol
cells.qualification: Constructive documentary direct-serial configuration, not a runtime measurement or radio-airtime bound. Retained configured callsigns/ports and a locked NET/ROM route (obs_count=0); learned sessions are recreated. One known adjacent peer, no digipeaters, no unrelated traffic or large route announcements, timely loss-free acknowledgments and timers preventing retry/poll bursts. Standard KISS without optional CRC-mode negotiation. No cryptographic authorization is supplied by this plaintext profile; retained labels/configuration do not imply authenticated peer identity. No IP encapsulation or application-layer fragmentation is introduced.

cells.reason: A supported Ethernet client can use the selected batman-adv native L2 service through an available access bridge. It retains its local MAC and known peer MAC; no endpoint IP, ARP or cryptographic session is added. Linux 6.12 soft-interface transmission learns the client source MAC before forwarding, and reception removes mesh encapsulation before delivering the native Ethernet frame. With the remote peer still available in the live mesh, two 256-byte native payload frames consume 2 x (256 + 14 + 4 + 8 + 12) = 588 endpoint byte-times. This meets the 65,536-byte F25 budget without keeping an endpoint session alive.
cells.method: Constructive documentary endpoint byte bound
cells.source_label: Pinned Linux 6.12 native Ethernet client and mesh-interface source
cells.qualification: Configured leaf-client witness, not a sleeping mesh-router bound. One untagged Ethernet access port bridges to bat0; mesh hard interfaces remain separate. The available infrastructure and active remote peer retain working reachability, while the returning client is relearned from its first frame. Use loop-free single-access bridges with bridge-loop-avoidance disabled, no STP/LLDP/IP services or unrelated traffic on the client link. Disablement is a disclosed configuration choice, not the kernel default. BATMAN_IV, native bonding and gateway-off choices remain; mesh OGM/translation-table traffic outside this endpoint interface is excluded by the approved F25 boundary. No claim of zero mesh overhead, peer cryptographic authorization, runtime measurement, energy or global capacity.

cells.reason: Use the already selected provisioned leaf LAN of the Babel-routed ULA hierarchy, consistent with D01-BL. Babel continues to maintain routes between infrastructure routers; the ordinary leaf endpoint does not become a Babel speaker. Allow 14 bounded IPv6 control frames for address checks, MLD reports/query, router discovery and neighbor-cache repair, each at most 256 byte-times including Ethernet overhead. Two IPv6 datagrams each carrying 256 useful bytes cost 334 byte-times each. Total upper bound: 4,252, below the 65,536-byte F25 budget.

Infrastructure is available as required by F25, but its control traffic outside this endpoint interface is not charged. Allow fresh neighbor discovery and address checks; finish before additional periodic maintenance or retries. No DNS, DHCP, TCP, TLS or cryptographic peer authentication is introduced. This is documentary plausibility for the existing leaf role, not a bound for a sleeping Babel transit router, arbitrary topology, energy or runtime performance.

cells.reason: A configured leaf can meet the approved F25 workload with its adjacent access router/root as the previously authorized peer. Count up to 14 neighbor/registration/RPL control datagrams, seven PSK DTLS handshake messages including optional cookie retry, seven ACK datagrams and two protected messages of 256 useful bytes each. With bounded options/identities every IPv6 datagram fits 640 bytes. Reserve ten 6LoWPAN fragments per datagram and 144 on-air bytes per fragment including PHY and link ACK. The conservative total is 43,200 bytes, below 65,536. Fresh DTLS and repaired network state are counted; no live session is reused.

A routed producer request therefore does not have a mechanism concealing its named target and producer provenance from that intermediary. This does not mean a Name is a host locator, that the signer is necessarily the serving node, or that the forwarder always knows a physical producer location. A cache can answer without contacting the producer, but absence of a live producer destination is not evidence that a contacted final endpoint is concealed. Consumer non-identification in C06 is a distinct property. No onion-routing or name-encryption extension is selected.

cells.reason: CORE can combine multiple small messages for the same adjacent peer into one plaintext buffer before encrypting it. When aggregation occurs, an outside observer sees the aggregate encrypted record rather than separate inner-message boundaries and emission times. This provides a limited batching mechanism under the existing C07 mechanism-presence rule. It is not padding, a constant-rate cover schedule, a randomized anonymity mix or a demonstrated reduction of end-to-end correlation. Total volume, aggregate timing and outer transport metadata remain observable; adjacent peers can decrypt their own CORE traffic. The feature is native CORE behavior, not anonymous file sharing or an added discovery/application protocol.
